abstract: Forecasting a curve, rather than a handful of scalar summaries of it, requires a notion of uncertainty that is itself functional. We propose FARCH, a functional nonlinear autoregressive model with conditional heteroscedasticity, in which the conditional mean and the conditional volatility of the next curve are forecasted jointly and nonparametrically, by reusing a single kernel weighting scheme --- built on a wavelet semi-metric between curves --- first on the curves themselves and then on their squared residuals. From this pair of estimators we derive two constructions of prediction bands: a pointwise band, obtained from marginal scenario quantiles, and a uniform, sup-norm band, calibrated for decisions that concern the entire forecasted path rather than any single instant. Applied to day-ahead forecasting of half-hourly French national electricity demand (1996--2009), and compared, under an identical protocol, against four existing prediction-interval constructions that do not model the conditional variance explicitly, the uniform FARCH band attains pointwise coverage statistically indistinguishable from its nominal target at the 80%, 90% and 95% levels, and a curve-wise coverage of 90.1%, significantly above the 70.8% reached by the best competing method, at the cost of a wider interval. Pointwise bands, in contrast, undercover regardless of whether the variance is modelled explicitly, indicating that state-dependent volatility and simultaneous calibration are two distinct ingredients that a trustworthy prediction band must combine.
